column1: # Player-facing settings: the Mac app's settings window (dm/mac/Launcher.swift) shows them before the game starts; Mac front ends read the same list.

# dm/games/settings.py writes one game's list into its app (dm/launcher.json; dm/mac/pack_app.py through scripts/build_app.py): the rows whose condition holds for that game, with its defaults. Each sets an environment variable the host reads when the game starts; one an env file sets
# (the player's env.txt, the bundle's dm/env.txt) is shown but kept. Diagnostic switches stay environment-only, so they are not listed here. The player's page is docs/settings.md.
#   variable  the environment variable the setting sets

#   kind      choice: values value=label,..., an option only some games have with ?<shown>&<shown> after its label (languages: the game's own, from its control data; every language when it has none, with a note); range: values low:high:step, shown as a percentage;
#             toggle: values - (on sets 1, off 0) or <on>/<off>, the two values the variable takes (on/off)
#   default   a value (a toggle's: 1 on, 0 off); DM_GAME_<NAME>: the host's own default from the game profile (game_profile.h, game.py); build:<VAR>: the build's setting (the packer's environment)

#   shown     always; DM_GAME_<NAME>!=<value> or ==<value>; fixups:<KEY>: main's rewriter table has that key (a stub in the game's build, patch_nso.py); languages>1 (more than one to pick, so also when the control data lists none);
#             mac-mic: a Mac app whose modules import the supported polling InputStream API;

#             practice: an app that carries the practice tools (Resources/dm/practice, which the host loads with DM_PRACTICE=1): the rewritten modules' practice/ has a rewritten module and an IPS (the packing script's practice_tools stage);
#   section   Game, Controls, Performance or Practice: a heading on the single settings screen. Rows appear in table order within each section
#             Reset to tested defaults clears all launcher choices; values fixed by an env file stay
#   label, note  the setting's name and the line under it (may be empty; only for a setting with a cost: latency, memory, heat)
#   meta      optional, key=value pairs separated by ; (settings.py META lists the keys; docs/frontends.md, The settings list, describes them):
#             level=basic  a setting a front end shows first;  needs=<VAR>=<value>  a sub-setting, drawn only while the row that sets <VAR> has that value

column8: Lets the game lower its resolution under load. Turn off to keep full resolution for the selected console mode.
Scales the finished picture to your screen. Uses more GPU time and can increase heat.
Replaces the game's own upscaler of the 3D scene. Saves GPU time; the picture looks different.
Plays Joy-Con 2 and Pro Controller 2 over Bluetooth: hold Sync on one during the game to pair it. macOS asks once for Bluetooth access.
Lets the game hear your microphone. macOS asks for access when you launch with this enabled.
Up to one frame more display latency.
Keeps a pipeline archive; uses more memory.
The first start waits a few minutes for it, once.
sloperinaGZ, the practice menu speedrunners use: hold R and push the right stick down in the game to open it. It changes the game's code; off, none of it is loaded.
